provenance: Telephone call, 2026-09-03, Larry's son asking the tier-1 questions from the interview guide and typing Larry's answers as he spoke them. The Camp Zama date question had been promoted to the head of the guide that morning. Raw capture: research/interviews/breakfast-questions.md, annotated in place under each question.
text: Kennedy pretty much ran the camp. When he was gone, Lowry ran the camp. Kennedy wasn't there that last week when all the shit happened. At night, normally looking into Cambodia to the West you might see 15 camp fires going, that week there must have been a hundreds and hundreds like the whole thing was lit up at night with camp fires. I figured they were all enemy fires on the Ho Chi Men trail. This was right before the battle of the I Drang Valley. We had Mohawk airplane flying this everynight with infared. He could have been taking pictures with the infared.
researchNotes: Asked open who else ran the camp, with no name supplied. Three things follow. First, it corroborates from a second direction his 2026-09-02 statement that "all the officers were gone" on the day of the accusation: Kennedy was absent that last week and Lowry was running the camp, which is why Lowry was the man on the other radio. Second, the campfires are new, and are the context nothing else has supplied for the "450 enemy digging in" - a normal night showed about fifteen fires westward toward Cambodia, and that week showed hundreds. Third, the OV-1 Mohawk flying nightly with infrared is a real and documented capability, and he raises unprompted the possibility that it, rather than a helicopter, was what detected the concentration he radioed; on 2026-09-02 he said a helicopter spotted them and that he never heard it, which fits a fixed-wing aircraft at night better than a helicopter. A TENSION recorded and not reconciled: he places this "right before the battle of the I Drang Valley", and Ia Drang was 14-18 November 1965, by which time he had been in Japan for over two months on his own dating. His spellings are preserved: "Ho Chi Men", "I Drang", "infared".
